analysis:
All changes are CI tooling for the advisory threat-model reviewer (.github/scripts). They do not touch the provider, coordinator, WebSocket, attestation, key or cache code that the canonical threat model covers (T-041 was supplied only as context). No threat IDs apply and I report no findings.

1) test-threat-model-review.py, head lines 732-757: the test now expects the scanner checkout to use ref default_branch, with the PR base SHA passed only as data through THREAT_REVIEW_BASE_SHA. It still forbids head.sha, head.ref and base.sha in the scanner checkout, and keeps persist-credentials false, the hash-pinned pip install, and the install-before-Bedrock-credentials ordering. The test therefore preserves the rule that PR-head code never runs in the secret-bearing pull_request_target job. The workflow YAML itself was not supplied, so the real checkout and env wiring are unverified.

2) threat-model-review.py line 22: run() is now called as run(event, os.environ) without Path.cwd(). The budget_runner implementation was not supplied, so I could not check where it now loads docs/threat-model.yaml from (default-branch checkout versus pinned base SHA). That affects review fidelity and is not a provider security regression.

3) bedrock.py head lines 103-110: the request adds outputConfig with a json_schema built by the new structured_output.bedrock_schema. Sol gets additionalModelRequestFields strict=True. The comment says the local validator still checks bounds, coverage and citations. structured_output.py was not supplied. Output remains untrusted model text, and last_request now records response_format.

The next pass should check the workflow YAML for checkout refs and secret exposure, and budget_runner.run for the new signature and the threat-model source.
